data.title: Regulation of cellular growth by the Drosophila target of rapamycin dTOR
data.authors: Zhang H; Stallock JP; Ng JC; Reinhard C; Neufeld TP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Drosophila melanogaster dTOR mutants and mosaic clones; PI3K activation in vivo; in vitro dTOR kinase assays on p70S6K; S6K and cyclin E overexpression rescue
data.finding: The authors showed that fly TOR (dTOR) is needed inside each cell for normal growth and proliferation during larval development. dTOR was also needed for the extra cell growth caused by activating PI3K signalling. As in mammalian cells, dTOR kinase activity was needed for growth factor-dependent phosphorylation of S6 kinase in vitro, and overexpressing S6 kinase rescued dTOR mutant flies to viability. dTOR loss also produced signs of amino acid starvation, such as smaller nucleoli and lipid droplet clumping in the fat body, plus a cell-type-specific cell cycle arrest that cyclin E could bypass. The authors proposed that dTOR links growth factor signalling to nutrient availability during development. Boundary: Drosophila larvae and in vitro kinase assays; rescue relied on overexpression of S6 kinase, and results are not shown in mammals here.
data.abstract_excerpt: The TOR protein kinases (TOR1 and TOR2 in yeast; mTOR/FRAP/RAFT1 in mammals) promote cellular proliferation in response to nutrients and growth factors, but their role in development is poorly understood. Here, we show that the Drosophila TOR homolog dTOR is required cell autonomously for normal growth and proliferation during larval development, and for increases in cellular growth caused by activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) signaling pathway.
